answer: Each agent must post a bond from an external, scarce resource before it can earn reputation or claim rewards; the protocol locks that stake and slashes it when fraud is proven. A sybil attacker can still create many identities, but each needs its own funded bond, so identities are not free. The anchor is the locked collateral, while onyx and quill can name two independent attestations required to prove fraud before slashing, limiting arbitrary punishment. The attacker pays capital costs and risks losing every exposed stake.
